newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, MAY 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, MAY 30.

text.p: The following are the highlights
of stories from the Irish press on Friday.
IRISH TIMES
- U.S. President Clinton's support for peace efforts raises Northern Ireland ceasefire hopes

- Shares in Ryanair shot up dramatically in Dublin and New York after pricing for the heavily oversubscribed offer was announced -The governor of the central bank has warned that interest rates may not fall substantially after monetary union - There was limited reaction to the growing perception that monetary union may not go ahead on time - Banks are charging special "arrangement fees" to people seeking to borrow money to buy Norwich Union shares
IRISH INDEPENDENT
- Government borrowing will be only half the previously expected level Finance Minister Ruairi Quinnn said
- The timetable for EMU was hanging in the balance as the controversy between the German government and the Bundesbank appreared to intensify
- Ryanair share price rises 60 percent on the first day of trading
- Fianna Fail winning war of words in general election campaign
- Shipping line Pandora sees an injunction against the Irish
Road Haulage Association preventing it from acting for Dublin
hauliers currently fighting for an increase in haulage rates
from the shippers in Dublin Port
THE EXAMINER
- Ryanair flotation earns 70 million punts for founding family
in just one day
- Bob Dylan fans will not get a refund on their tickets for a
Cork concert after his withdrawal after suffering heart problems
- Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams praises President Clinton's
balanced support in peace quest
-- Dublin newsroom +353 1 661 3377
